title: Atlas appliance — evening runbook & quick notes
content:
Evening on-site scratchpad — Atlas appliance (customer: MedAxis)

Context:
- On-prem preview install 11/20-11/21. Single Atlas 2U node + customer infra (vSphere, internal DNS, corp-firewall).
- Objective tonight: finish config drift fixes, validate model serving on local GPU, hand off morning checklist to CS.

Quick summary / headline issues:
1) Host network needed extra static route to reach KMS (customer firewall); required customer FW rule add.
2) NTP was 20s off — caused cert validation flakiness for Control Plane registration.
3) Kernel CVE patch applied; node reboot triggered systemd timeout for redis.service (sticky).

TODO (short, actionable) — run before EOD:
- [x] Confirm firewall rule applied (customer ticket #4521) — RTT to kms.redwood.internal OK
- [x] Re-sync NTP and monitor for 15m (chronyd)
- [x] Re-run host registration: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/register-host --tenant medaxis
- [ ] Restart redis and check persistence: sudo systemctl restart redwood-redis.service; tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/redis.log
- [ ] Smoke test model (gpt-small-open) locally with stress of 3 concurrent inferences: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-small-open","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":8}'
- [ ] Dump kernel logs: sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 100 > /tmp/agent-journal-eod.log
- [ ] Snapshot disk usage for /var/lib/redwood (in case quant files balloon)

Notes / Commands I kept running:
- check net routes: ip route show table all | grep 10.8.0.0/16
- test KMS reachability: nc -vz kms.redwood.internal 443  (had to ask customer to open outbound)
- docker images: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/containerctl images | grep quant
- GPU check: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv

Observations + debugging log snippets (from today):
- 18:12 — control plane refused registration: x509: certificate is valid for agent.redwood, not atlas.medaxis.internal -> caused by internal DNS not providing expected CNAME. Workaround: set /etc/hosts entry for controlplane.redwood.internal -> registration proceeded. Need to remove before handing off (temp).
- 19:03 — redis persistent save failed: RDB snapshot aborted: background save in progress. Manual restart cleared it but verify dump file integrity.

Customer environment reminders (non-blockers):
- vSphere: nested VLANs for management network; IP scopes vary between racks A/B. Avoid pushing DHCP leases in management range.
- KMS sits behind corporate proxy (explicit) -> we use customer-managed proxy creds (stored in /etc/redwood/proxy.conf but note proxy requires username formatted as DOMAIN\\svc-redwood).
- HSM is not in scope for this trial; keys are wrapped via KMS software only.

Risks / follow-ups for tomorrow:
- Remove temporary /etc/hosts entry and validate DNS fix from customer (DNS team to add CNAME) — might break control-plane re-registration if DNS not ready. Owner: Riley
- Add systemd RestartSec tweak for redwood-redis to reduce downtime on reboot. Owner: Samira
- Follow up on disk snapshot retention policy: quant files trend large on v1.9.3 models. Consider rotating older quant artifacts to object storage. Owner: Jordan

Meeting / handoff notes to leave in morning: (short bullet list to paste into CS handoff)
- Status: Node healthy, registered with control plane, NTP drift fixed. Redis restarted successfully but please watch for RDB save warnings in logs.
- Known temp tweak: /etc/hosts for controlplane.redwood.internal present (remove after DNS fix).
- Next steps: run smoke model test at 0900, confirm canary rollout of gpt-small-open to tenant medaxis.
- Contact: Riley (oncall tonight until 23:00 PST), Samira (AM follow-up)

Open questions / brain-dump (unstructured):
- Should we bake a small preflight that checks NTP, DNS canonical names, and KMS reachability before attempting registration? Might save a 30–60m loop on field installs.
- Consider an auto-recovery handler for redis timeouts that will try graceful BGSAVE and then restart if blocked > 60s.
- Customer asked about offline model loading (airgap): need short doc for step-by-step unzip -> quant load -> signature check. Could draft tomorrow.

Raw links / tickets referenced:
- PRIV-4521 (customer firewall)
- slack thread: #onprem-medaxis-deploy (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C07DEPLOY)

End-of-day quick metrics snapshot:
- GPU util (last 10 min): 12%, 0% memory pressure
- Disk free /var/lib/redwood: 820GB / 1.2TB
- Uptime since last reboot: 3h 12m (kernel updated earlier today)

If anything regresses overnight ping customer NOC (noc@medaxis.com) first, then escalate to Riley.

-- Jordan
(quick notes, not final runbook)
